LESSON: MODELLING AND ORNAMENT MAKING.

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.6: Modelling and Ornament Making.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Modelling and Ornament Making., part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How are ornaments made?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Modelling and Ornament Making. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner work together prepare clay or papier mache for modelling items

• Creativity and imagination: The learner creates make a single stranded necklace and a matching bracelet,

Values:
• Respect: The learner gives positive feedback as they display items made.

• Unity: The learner in groups in groups, prepare clay or papier mache for modelling items.

• Patriotism: The learner takes pride in making ornaments using recyclable materials from the local community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Safety and security: The learner observes their safety as they fire the clay beads in an improvised kiln.

• Social cohesion: The learner portrays team spirit as they explore pinch and pellet technique to make simple forms in pairs.

Link to other subjects:

Environmental Activities: The learner applies knowledge and skills gained in Environmental Activities to create melodic

patterns from differently pitched objects such as voiced or tuned percussion.
